Chicago, winter of 1945. The city is frozen under a sheet of ice, but inside a quiet apartment on the north side… something very dark was being uncovered.
Detectives enter an apartment, push open the door and just stop.

The air is still and thick. The room smells like iron, something sickly sweet. And then detectives see it. On the wall, scrawled in janky ass writing, there's a message written in the victims red lipstick saying: 
“For heaven’s sake catch me before I kill more. I cannot control myself.”

Was it a confession? A warning? And the biggest question, what if they meant it? It's a message that would send the city into full blown panic and launch a manhunt for a killer who, even after being caught, would leave people thinking, was that the right guy? 
Today we are talking about The Lipstick Killer.

Previous fingerprint technician here!

Sadly this technology has not evolved too terribly much. We still use minutae aka finger points to make matches. The more degraded the print, the harder it is to identify these points.

We rely alot on juries believing expert testimony, as fingerprint examination is not an exact science. You could match minutae on a print and claim it is a match and yet there are plenty of prints that could match it that aren't that individual's. There have been many cases of incorrect identification with prints.

Adding to the complexity of this, prints can and will change over time (skin on fingers shrinking and/or moving, burns, scars, etc.).
